name: Citation Graphs Over Time
title: Citation Graphs Over Time
answer: Citation graphs over time trace how papers, authors, and ideas influence one another across months and years. In this site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims, such graphs show which older works remain cited and which newer works redirect attention. The temporal view matters because a citation is not only a link but an event with a date, and the order of those events changes how a field is understood.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Citation graphs over time trace how papers, authors, and ideas influence one another across months and years. In this site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims, such graphs show which older works remain cited and which newer works redirect attention. The temporal view matters because a citation is not only a link but an event with a date, and the order of those events changes how a field is understood.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Citation graphs over time run on graph databases that store nodes for papers and edges for citations, with timestamps on each edge. Reference parsers extract bibliographic data from PDFs and metadata feeds, and persistent identifiers such as DOIs keep nodes stable as versions change. Temporal indexes allow queries that filter edges by year or month without rebuilding the whole graph.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins by extracting references from full text and matching them to existing records, resolving author and venue ambiguities. Analysts then build directed edges with publication dates and slice the graph into time windows to observe how clusters form, merge, or fade. Common measures include citation half-life, growth rate of a paper's incoming edges, and bursts where a work suddenly gains many citations after a delay.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Citation graphs inherit rights and coverage limits from their source databases, so provenance must record which index supplied each reference and when it was retrieved. A graph built only from one publisher or language will undercount work from other communities, and automated reference matching can silently merge distinct authors or split one author's name. On this site, links always point to the original paper rather than a search aggregator, which keeps the trail of evidence direct and auditable.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Citation graphs over time are moving toward continuously updated temporal knowledge graphs that ingest new preprints and retractions within days rather than months. Better author and institution disambiguation, including ORCID and ROR identifiers, will reduce false merges and splits. Open citation datasets and shared graph schemas may make longitudinal studies reproducible across fields, while dynamic network models begin to predict which older papers will regain attention.
